h1: The 8 Best Fast Printers for Home Offices of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaTitle: Best Fast Office Printers 2026: Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: eight fast printers for home offices, from a 35 PPM color laser to budget inkjets, with advice on duplex, volume and ink costs.
summary: The Canon MF753Cdw II is our top pick for sustained speed, at a rated 35 pages per minute. The Brother HL-L3220CDW is the cheaper color laser, and the Brother DCP-L2640DW is the pick for mono documents. The Epson EcoTank ET-4800 suits high-volume inkjet users, and the HP DeskJet 4355 covers light use.
intro: Page-per-minute ratings flatter printers, because the number describes pages after the first one. If you mostly send single pages now and then, the wait for the first page and the warm-up matter far more than the headline speed.

We ranked eight printers on rated speed where the listing gives one, duplex support, paper handling, connectivity and how each suits your printing habit. Laser ranks high for volume, and inkjet gets credit for color and low entry cost. Treat every PPM as a rated figure rather than a measured result.

products.name: Canon Color imageCLASS MF753Cdw II Wireless Duplex Laser Printer
products.verdict: The fastest rated color laser here, built for steady volume.
products.description:
The MF753Cdw II is a color laser multifunction rated at 35 pages per minute, with automatic duplex, scan, copy and fax, an automatic document feeder and wireless connectivity. It carries a three-year limited warranty and lands in the $200 to $500 range.

It ranks first because it combines the highest rated speed on this list with an automatic document feeder for multi-page scans. The Brother HL-L3220CDW is far cheaper to run but rated at roughly half the speed, which is the tradeoff you accept.

Choose it for steady printing volume. The caveat is size and cost, since a color laser multifunction takes real desk space.
products.idealFor: Home offices that print high volumes regularly.
products.skipIf: You print a few pages a week.

products.name: Brother HL-L3220CDW Color Laser Printer
products.verdict: Laser speed and a big paper tray without top-tier pricing.
products.description:
The HL-L3220CDW is a color laser rated at 19 pages per minute with automatic duplex printing, a 250-sheet tray, wireless and mobile printing. It lands in the $200 to $500 range.

It ranks second because the rated speed is lower than the Canon's, and it is print-only, so it has no scanner. In return you get a large tray that cuts refilling and a simpler machine.

Pick it if you want laser reliability without a multifunction. The caveat is that it cannot scan or copy.
products.idealFor: Print-only offices wanting color laser without extras.
products.skipIf: You need scanning or an automatic document feeder.

products.name: Brother DCP-L2640DW Wireless Compact Monochrome Multi-Function Laser Printer
products.verdict: A compact mono laser that is quick off the mark for short jobs.
products.description:
A compact monochrome laser multifunction with copy, scan and duplex, wireless and mobile printing, Alexa voice support and a fast warm-up for intermittent printing. It lands in the $200 to $500 range.

It ranks third because black-and-white only limits it against the color picks above, yet the quick warm-up suits people who print a page or two at a time. Against the Canon, you give up color and rated speed in exchange for a smaller machine.

Choose it for contracts, forms and everyday documents. The caveat is that no color pages are possible.
products.idealFor: Desks with short, frequent print jobs.

products.name: Brother INKvestment 5010 Wireless Color Inkjet All-in-One Printer
products.verdict: Color inkjet with two-sided copying and scanning built in.
products.description:
A color inkjet all-in-one with automatic duplex printing, automatic two-sided copy and scan, a 2.7 inch touchscreen and wireless connectivity. It uses an INKvestment ink tank cartridge system and lands in the $200 to $500 range.

It ranks fourth because it matches the laser units on duplex scanning but is not rated for page speed in the listing. It sits above the cheaper inkjets thanks to the two-sided scan, which saves time on paper-heavy tasks.

Buy it for mixed color and document work. The caveat is that you pay laser prices for an inkjet.
products.idealFor: Offices copying and scanning two-sided pages in color.
products.skipIf: A rated page speed is your priority.

products.name: Epson EcoTank ET-4800 Wireless All-in-One Cartridge-Free Supertank Printer
products.verdict: Refillable ink bottles mean fewer stops in the middle of a job.
products.description:
A cartridge-free ink tank all-in-one with an automatic document feeder, Ethernet and wireless connectivity, and built-in scan, copy and fax. You refill from bottles instead of swapping cartridges. It lands in the $100 to $200 range.

It ranks fifth because the listing gives no rated speed, and the tank design is about low interruptions rather than raw pace. Compared with the Brother INKvestment, it costs less and adds an Ethernet port.

Choose it for regular multi-page jobs where running out of ink mid-run is the annoyance. The caveat is that inkjet output is slower than laser at volume.
products.idealFor: Regular multi-page jobs with fewer ink interruptions.
products.skipIf: You want the fastest laser output.

products.name: Brother Work Smart 1360 Wireless Color Inkjet All-in-One Printer
products.verdict: Lets you trade print quality for speed when you are in a hurry.
products.description:
A color inkjet all-in-one with automatic duplex, a 1.8 inch display, multiple print quality modes and a Refresh Subscription trial. It lands in the $100 to $200 range.

It ranks sixth because the display is smaller than the INKvestment's and the listing gives no rated speed. The quality modes are the useful part, since a draft mode can finish a routine page quicker.

Pick it for jobs that mix quick drafts and finished color. The caveat is that the included subscription is a trial.
products.skipIf: You want a document feeder or rated speed.

products.name: Canon PIXMA TR4720 All-in-One Wireless Printer
products.verdict: A compact inkjet with a feeder for light daily printing.
products.description:
A compact color inkjet all-in-one with an automatic document feeder, mobile printing and a legacy fax feature, plus wireless connectivity. It lands in the $50 to $100 range.

It ranks seventh because it targets single pages throughout the day, not volume, and the listing offers no speed figure. Against the HP DeskJet, the feeder is the practical gain.

Choose it for occasional document jobs. The caveat is that it is not built for large batches.
products.idealFor: Single pages through the day in a small office.

products.name: HP DeskJet 4355 Wireless All-in-One Color Inkjet Printer
products.verdict: The cheapest way into home printing, not a speed pick.
products.description:
A compact color inkjet that prints, scans and copies, with a three-month Instant Ink trial, a simple wireless setup flow and optional AI-capable printing features. It lands in the $50 to $100 range.

It ranks last because it has no feeder, no duplex mention and no speed figure in the listing. What it offers is a low cost of entry.

Buy it for light, occasional printing on a tight budget. The caveat is that it does not belong in a list about speed except as a fallback.
products.idealFor: Light printing on a tight budget.
products.skipIf: You value speed or print in volume.

whatMatters.detail: Pages per minute is how many pages a printer outputs after it starts. It matters for long jobs but not for one-page prints. Look for the PPM figure in the specs.
Laser uses toner and tends to be faster for text at volume. Inkjet costs less upfront and handles photos. Check the type in the title.
Automatic duplex prints on both sides without you flipping paper. It halves paper use and saves time. Look for automatic duplex rather than manual.
A feeder scans multi-page originals without placing each page by hand. It saves minutes on every scan job. Search for ADF in the listing.
Tanks and bottles lower the interruptions from empty cartridges. Subscriptions can add a monthly cost. Read how the supply is described.

cards.label: Laser
cards.text: Faster for documents and steadier at volume. The Canon MF753Cdw II, Brother HL-L3220CDW and DCP-L2640DW are the picks.

cards.label: Inkjet
cards.text: Lower entry cost and good color. The Epson ET-4800, Brother INKvestment and Work Smart cover it.

howToChoose.note: Most home offices that value speed should default to laser.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A fast warm-up so the first page comes out quickly.

cards.label: In this ranking
cards.text: The Brother DCP-L2640DW lists fast warm-up for intermittent printing.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You print in volume. The Canon MF753Cdw II carries the highest rated speed.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You print a few pages a week. The HP DeskJet 4355 or Canon PIXMA TR4720 is enough.

faq.q: Is a higher PPM always better?
faq.a: Only for long jobs. For one or two pages, warm-up and first-page time matter more than the rated speed.

faq.q: What is the most common printer mistake?
faq.a: Buying a cheap inkjet for volume. The savings upfront disappear when you replace ink often.

faq.q: Is a laser worth it over inkjet?
faq.a: If you print text regularly, yes. The Canon MF753Cdw II and Brother lasers suit steady use.
Several list mobile printing, including the Brother HL-L3220CDW and Canon PIXMA TR4720. Confirm the app on the listing.

faq.q: How do I cut interruptions from empty ink?
faq.a: Choose a tank design such as the Epson EcoTank ET-4800, which uses refillable bottles.

faq.q: Does the Instant Ink trial cost anything?
faq.a: The HP lists a three-month trial. Read the terms before continuing, since it becomes a subscription.

finalTake: For a home office that prints steadily, the Canon MF753Cdw II is the fastest rated option here. The Brother HL-L3220CDW is a cheaper laser, and the DCP-L2640DW fits short mono jobs. Inkjet buyers should look at the Epson EcoTank ET-4800.
